correctness.rationale: The seminorm calculation is correct. Nifa's peripheral description sends the tangent coordinates to \(\lambda\) and \(\lambda^{-N}\), so \(a[\lambda_r]+b[s_r]\) represents \(\lambda^{a-Nb}\). Nifa's Theorem 6.5 proves \(\operatorname{scl}(\lambda^N)=(N-1)/2\) and also realizes \(\lambda\) as a commutator. Homogeneity gives \(\operatorname{scl}(\lambda^{a-Nb})=(N-1)|a-Nb|/(2N)\). Liu--Ni--Sun--Wang's Remark 4.5 identifies their slope seminorm with stable commutator length and extends it to real homology. The kernel and strip follow immediately. The submitted unstable sublattice formula agrees exactly with Nifa's Remark 6.8.

originality.rationale: The stable formula is a direct corollary of two published statements read in full. Liu--Ni--Sun--Wang identify the induced slope seminorm with stable commutator length. Nifa supplies the full peripheral exponent \(b-Nq\), proves \(\operatorname{scl}(\lambda^N)=(N-1)/2\), and proves \(\lambda\) is a commutator. Homogeneity of stable commutator length then mechanically gives the submitted absolute-value seminorm; its kernel, unit strip and independence of the filling index are immediate algebraic consequences. Moreover, Nifa's Remark 6.8 already states the exact unstable singular-genus formula on precisely the submitted index-N sublattice. Therefore the final claim is covered by prior implication even though the word 'seminorm' does not appear in Nifa's paper.
